a_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM ↓ SOURCE ↓ GRADE ↓ FORMAL MEANING ↓ ARCHITECTURAL MEANING ↓ EXAMPLE ↓ LIMITATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Edition-2 book-writing methodology for a mentor role: before writing a chapter, ask what the reader must learn, the chapter's boundary, its authoritative sources, existing mathematical/formal material, what is established vs open, which findings affect the chapter, and which interfaces with previous chapters must stay consistent. During writing, follow the chain CLAIM -> SOURCE -> GRADE -> FORMAL MEANING -> ARCHITECTURAL MEANING -> EXAMPLE -> LIMITATION. After writing, run provenance, terminology, mathematical-strength, architecture-boundary, open-question, running-example, relation-status, no-hindsight, and forbidden-status-vocabulary checks, rerun after any substantive edit. When a difficult concept is encountered, the only permitted choices are: EXPLAIN EXISTING MODEL, EXPOSE OPEN QUESTION, REPORT FINDING, or REQUEST GOVERNANCE -- never 'INVENT A BETTER ARCHITECTURE' without an explicit research/governance commission.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

b_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
b_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Computable ≠ Implementable in principle but Computable = effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics. It also explicitly forbids calling something computable merely because a program could approximate it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Precise computability criterion: a predicate/function/relation/operation is computable only if it is an effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics (defined inputs/types, termination, deterministic result; for transformations, also a defined domain and codomain) — explicitly distinct from and stronger than mere in-principle implementability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Class A — directly computable ... Class B — computable only after semantic parameters are supplied ... Class C — not computable as currently defined ... Authoritative(x) Relevant(x) Correct(x) Adequate(x) when no operational decision procedure or authoritative source is defined.
a_rows_sample.statement: The theory's predicates/operations are sorted into three computability classes: Class A directly computable (structural parsing, identifier lookup, hashing, canonical serialization, deterministic transformation on fixed inputs), Class B computable only once semantic parameters are supplied (ValidOperation(D,o) needs a scale/type registry; Resolve(pi) needs a provenance registry), and Class C not computable as currently defined (Authoritative(x), Relevant(x), Correct(x), Adequate(x) — predicates with no operational decision procedure, exposing hidden human judgment).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity membership = UNDER-SPECIFIED unless an explicit ontology/registration boundary is introduced. ... Entity definition is conceptually clear but Entity membership is not universally decidable. ... Dimension: StructuralValidDimension(D) is computable ... but Structural validity ≠ Semantic adequac
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-object computability audit for Entity, Dimension, Value and Proposition: Entity's semantic definition ('subject of knowledge') is conceptually clear but membership is not universally decidable without an explicit ontology/registration boundary; Dimension's structural validity is computable but semantic adequacy is not; Value membership is computable only where its value space V_D has an effective representation, ranging from trivially decidable (finite sets) through grammar-parseable (formal version strings) to fundamentally undecidable (open-ended conceptual domains); Proposition well-formedness is therefore CONDITIONALLY COMPUTABLE, contingent on all three membership predicates being computable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValidation(A) can be computable, while Truth(A) cannot be assumed computable. ... Finite Status Algebra ⇒ Computable transition validation. But that does not make the assignment of the status computable. ... TransitionValidity ≠ StatusAssignment. This is one of the most important hidden bo
a_rows_sample.statement: Two of the audit's sharpest distinctions: (1) an Assertion's structural validation is computable while its Truth is not assumed computable; (2) given a finite epistemic-status algebra, mechanically validating whether a status TRANSITION is legal is computable, but this does NOT make the ASSIGNMENT of a status to an assertion (whether evidence actually warrants that status) computable — TransitionValidity != StatusAssignment is named one of the most important hidden boundaries in the whole theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralEquality = COMPUTABLE under canonical representation. ... SemanticEquality = CONDITIONAL not universally established [3m/300cm needs unit normalization; conceptual entities may need an ontology/identity registry]. ... IdentityConstruction can be computable, while IdentityResolution may rem
a_rows_sample.statement: Equality, identity, and provenance are each split into a computable mechanical half and a conditional/non-computable semantic half: structural equality is computable via canonicalization+hashing while semantic equality is only conditionally computable (domain-dependent, e.g. unit normalization for 3m vs 300cm); identity CONSTRUCTION (deterministic hashing of canonical data) is computable while identity RESOLUTION (whether two independently-supplied references denote the same real-world entity) may remain externally supplied or human-governed; provenance-reference LOOKUP is computable under three infrastructure assumptions, but this never establishes ProvenanceTruth — lookup is not validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay = Conditionally Computable [K0 persisted; every Ti defined; every input available; operation versions fixed; preconditions satisfied; operations deterministic]. ... Replayability ⇒ Immutable or versioned transformation semantics. ... Replay ≠ Reversal. Replay means reconstructing the forward
a_rows_sample.statement: Replay is conditionally computable under six named preconditions, and is proven to REQUIRE operation versioning (since changing an operation's semantics between (T1^2026) and (T1^2027) could replay the same history to different states, replayability implies immutable-or-versioned transformation semantics); Replay is also proven distinct from Reversal — if T is many-to-one (K1!=K2 but T(K1)=T(K2)), no inverse can uniquely reconstruct the original state, so Replay only reconstructs the forward computation, it does not recover an original state from an output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K* = coarsest sufficient state abstraction. But can we compute K*? In general, this is not automatically decidable. ... Minimality = NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED. This is not a defect in the theory. It is a correct research status. ... TestMinimal(K) [testing removals can discover counterexamples]
a_rows_sample.statement: Minimality (computing the coarsest sufficient K*) is found NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED, explicitly classified as a correct research status rather than a defect, requiring five unmet conditions (candidate abstraction, complete operation set, defined equivalence relation, sufficiency proof, strict-reduction-breaks-sufficiency proof); a further distinction is drawn between TestMinimal(K) (removal testing, which can find counterexamples) and ProveMinimal(K) (a full proof), since finite removal testing can never prove no future operation will require a removed component — empirical minimality evidence is not a mathematical minimality proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance decision = possibly non-computable input. ... Evidence handling is computable in layers [Retrieve(e), Hash(e), Link(A,e) computable; Assess(e,A) may require a human or statistical model]. ... StatisticalFormula ≠ ComputableKnowledgeOSQuantity ... Probability claims = UNDER-SPECIFIED unles
a_rows_sample.statement: Policy/authority, evidence, statistics and uncertainty are each shown to contain a non-computable normative core: Authorize(actor,action,policy) is decidable only if policy is fully formalized as rules, otherwise it is a possibly non-computable governance-decision input; evidence handling is computable in layers (retrieval/hashing/linkage computable, but Assess(e,A) may require a human or statistical model); a statistical formula's mere existence (e.g. Bayes' rule) does not make a KnowledgeOS quantity computable — a probability claim is UNDER-SPECIFIED without an explicit probability space (Omega,F,P); and Uncertainty is not computable until its semantics are fixed, since a bare number like U(A)=0.2 could mean probability, confidence, epistemic strength, error bound, entropy, or subjective belief — mathematically different things.

Truth of arbitrary assertion 🔴 ... Relevance 🔴 ... Correctness 🔴 ... Adequacy 🔴 ... Minimality proof 🔴 ... Uncertainty semantics 🔴 ... Stati
a_rows_sample.statement: A 23-row 'hidden human judgment map' rates every major KnowledgeOS concept's current computability from green (canonical serialization, structural equality, hash identity, registry lookup, finite status membership) through yellow (typed proposition validation, value-space membership, provenance lookup, deterministic replay, transition validation, semantic equality) to red (entity identity resolution, status assignment, evidence assessment, authority determination, policy interpretation, truth, relevance, correctness, adequacy, minimality proof, uncertainty semantics, statistical quantities without a model) — presented as the step's most valuable single output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL / DETERMINISTIC CORE [typing, identity references, canonicalization, equality, membership, transition validation, replay, hashing] ... EXTERNAL / PARAMETRIC SEMANTICS [policy, evidence, time, provenance store, authority, measurement regime] ... NORMATIVE / ASSESSMENT BOUNDARY [truth assessmen
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-layer architecture is derived from the audit: a FORMAL/DETERMINISTIC CORE (typing, identity references, canonicalization, equality, membership, transition validation, replay, hashing), an EXTERNAL/PARAMETRIC SEMANTICS layer (policy, evidence, time, provenance store, authority, measurement regime), and a NORMATIVE/ASSESSMENT BOUNDARY (truth assessment, relevance, adequacy, authority assignment, epistemic judgment, unresolved statistical assumptions) — explicitly not excluding the bottom layer from KnowledgeOS, only forbidding it from being falsely represented as purely deterministic without an actual decision procedure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ValueObject from DomainDecision from ExternalPolicy from Assessment. A DDD system should not hide a human governance decision inside a method named isValid() if the result actually depends on an unmodeled authority judgment. That would violate the Ubiquitous Language boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation of the three-layer architecture: the domain model must distinguish ValueObject from DomainDecision from ExternalPolicy from Assessment, and must never hide a human governance decision inside an innocuously-named method like isValid() when the result actually depends on unmodeled authority judgment, which would violate the Ubiquitous Language boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS can be computationally rigorous without claiming that all knowledge judgment is computable. This is actually stronger than attempting to make everything deterministic. ... ComputableCore ... JudgmentBoundary. The deterministic core can then guarantee: given the same formal inputs, the sa
a_rows_sample.statement: The step's most important finding: KnowledgeOS can be computationally rigorous WITHOUT claiming all knowledge judgment is computable — a stronger, more defensible architecture than attempting universal determinism; the theory should explicitly separate a ComputableCore (guaranteeing the same result from the same formal inputs) from a JudgmentBoundary (guaranteeing only that a decision is recorded, attributed, contextualized, and auditable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate: Computability Boundary Principle. Let T:X×C→Y ... If [effective representations; decidable preconditions; terminating algorithm; deterministic external interfaces] then T is computable relative to C. But if T depends on an undefined judgment predicate J(x), then T is not established as co
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate 'Computability Boundary Principle' theorem is proposed: an operation T:X x C -> Y is computable relative to C if X,C,Y have effective representations, all preconditions are decidable, T is a terminating algorithm, and all external dependencies have deterministic interfaces; if T depends on an undefined judgment predicate, T is not computable until that predicate is formalized — generalized as Computability(T) requires Computability of all of T's semantic dependencies, explicitly flagged as a derived candidate, not yet a proven corpus theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The correct question is: Which information must be represented in the deterministic state so that every deterministic operation is computable? and separately: Which decisions remain explicit external/normative inputs? ... Computability of candidate K ≠ Sufficiency of candidate K. Both gates must eve
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel-minimality research question: rather than asking whether the WHOLE theory can be made computable, the correct questions are which information must sit in the deterministic state for every deterministic operation to be computable, and which decisions should remain explicit external/normative inputs — with computability of a candidate K explicitly kept distinct from its sufficiency; both gates must eventually pass independently.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The existence of formal notation does not imply computability. ... Relevant(A) is a syntactically valid mathematical predicate. But unless Relevant has a decision procedure, it remains semantically under-specified. Likewise Minimal(K) can be written mathematically without being decidable. Likewise T
a_rows_sample.statement: Critical negative result: formal mathematical notation for a predicate (Relevant(A), Minimal(K), Truth(A)) does not by itself imply computability — each remains semantically under-specified or merely meaningful, not decidable/computable, unless an actual decision procedure is supplied; this falsifies the implicit assumption that writing something mathematically is the same as making it computable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DECIDABLE / COMPUTABLE / PARAMETRIC / HUMAN-ASSESSABLE / UNDER-SPECIFIED. This is preferable to repeatedly using the vague word: valid. ... StructuralValid(A) may be DECIDABLE. While EpistemicallyValid(A) may be HUMAN-ASSESSABLE until a formal assessment model exists.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes replacing the overloaded word 'valid' throughout the theory's vocabulary with a five-value computability-classification label attached to every important predicate: DECIDABLE, COMPUTABLE, PARAMETRIC, HUMAN-ASSESSABLE, or UNDER-SPECIFIED (e.g. StructuralValid(A) is DECIDABLE, while EpistemicallyValid(A) is HUMAN-ASSESSABLE until a formal assessment model exists).

a_rows_sample.statement: Step 266 final verdict: COMPUTABILITY PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED, NOT CLOSED — structural computation, typed validation (where domains are formalized), deterministic replay (with versioned operations), and provenance lookup (with stable references) are closed/strongly established; semantic equality, entity identity resolution, assessment/status assignment, policy/authority semantics, uncertainty, minimality, and a complete executable operation registry all remain not closed.

a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up Step 267 with a seven-value theory-to-implementation correspondence classification scheme (IMPLEMENTED, PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, SIMULATED, TESTED, UNTESTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, NO CORRESPONDING OBJECT), reframing the empirical question from 'does KnowledgeOS implement the theory' to 'for each formal object, what in the actual system realizes it and what evidence proves the correspondence'.

Five distinct mathematical objections, each correct: A proposition is not a subset of Ω. e∈𝓕 is a type error. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Traces ARC A (measure theory): the original 2026-08-25 proposal to treat knowledge as a measurable space/projection-as-measure was refuted just seven minutes later by five correct mathematical objections (a proposition is not a subset of the sample space; confidence/relevance/stability/attention are not countably additive so are not measures; the divergence PDE needs geometry the bare measurable space lacks; TV/Wasserstein/JS/KL divergences are not interchangeable; the Alignment=1-distance formula is invalid across different distance ranges) — all independently verified correct by this session.

b_rows_sample.statement: A second, six-part round of category errors (found the same day) further dismantled a stochastic-filtering reformulation of knowledge: conflating the domain and epistemic state spaces, treating a filtration as knowledge itself, presupposing an undefined X_t inside a conditional expectation, conflating differing information with differing probability measures across agents, misreading Radon-Nikodym incomparability as epistemic incomparability, and mistaking specific stochastic-process properties (martingale, submartingale, quadratic variation, Ito SDEs) for general epistemic properties (stability, learning, noise, evolution law).

b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-B3, directly qualifying the K=(A,R) minimality narrative used throughout this batch: the terminal K=(A,R) is strictly poorer in stated components than earlier Q6/Q13 candidates (which carried evidence, history, zero-findings and lineage as first-class parts of K itself); the reduction to (A,R) worked by relocating those components elsewhere (into Assertion internals, external History, external Policy), but the relocation targets were fixed AFTER the reduction rather than justified before it, and whether (A,R) is actually SUFFICIENT is exactly the still-open Step 259/260 congruence question.

b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-C1: the corpus's evidence-qualification rule (relevance to a proposition under an explicit rule) and its own later computability audit (Step 266, classifying Relevant(A) as non-computable as currently specified) are logically connected — the qualification rule's load-bearing predicate is exactly the one later shown undecidable — yet no document anywhere in the 270-step, 3-day-separated corpus ever connects these two results, so 'evidence is closed' (Closure-04) and 'relevance is open' (Step 266) coexist unreconciled.

Separation: CORPUS ESTABLISHES | Vocabulary: UNRESOLVED. Superseded, Invalidated, Contested and Conflicted are each assigned to different axes in dif
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC D: the Epistemic-Status/Governance-Status orthogonality is confirmed CORPUS ESTABLISHES (admission is not a truth function; an assertion can be admitted while weak/contested/wrong), but the actual vocabulary membership remains UNRESOLVED — terms like Superseded, Invalidated, Contested, and Conflicted are inconsistently assigned to one axis or the other across different corpus documents.

Reflexivity PROVISIONALLY DERIVED ... symmetry and transitivity DERIVED under ordinary equality. This session checked the three proofs: they are correct but tri
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC E (State vs History, called 'the deepest and most honest arc') is independently checked and found genuinely sound where claimed: semantic minimality is correctly distinguished from mere syntactic compactness; the requirement that the equivalence relation be a congruence (not merely an equivalence) for the transformation set is correctly derived; the reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity proofs are verified correct but trivial (holding for any observational equivalence, establishing nothing KnowledgeOS-specific) — and importantly, the corpus itself does not overclaim them; hash identity is correctly kept distinct from semantic identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-E1 (DERIVED, CRITICAL). Step 260.16: membership requires the equivalence test — H∈[H₀] ⟺ H≡H₀. Step 260.9: ≡ quantifies over the whole transformation algebra 𝒯. Step 266: 𝒯 is not closed. Therefore ≡ is defined by a universal quantification over a set that has never been enumerated. It is not mer
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-E1 (CRITICAL), sharper than the corpus's own Step 260 gate: since the semantic-equivalence relation equiv is defined by universal quantification over the mandatory transformation algebra T, and T itself is not closed/fully enumerated (per Step 266), equiv is not merely undecidable — it is NOT YET A WELL-DEFINED RELATION, because its defining quantifier ranges over an open, unenumerated collection; every object depending on it (the minimal quotient K*, membership A in K, state equality K1=K2, and the Step 259 sufficiency/congruence theorem) inherits this indeterminacy, undermining the confidence level of the congruence-based results relied on throughout the batch's canonical-K work.

The regime shift at ~Step 213 is the corpus's most
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC F identifies three successive method regimes across the corpus's history: F1 lens-driven (philosophical/scriptural lenses through step ~158), F2 formal build-out (algebras, type systems, architecture through step 215), and F3 archaeology-and-audit (the corpus turning on itself, steps 213-270) — the F1-to-F3 transition is self-diagnosed within the corpus itself, at step 236, explicitly titled 'We Have a Problem With the Existing Reconstruction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-F2 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL). F3 audits by reading, never by running. Across all 270 steps and 550 files there are zero executable artifacts (INV-9). Steps titled 'Executable Knowledge State Model', 'Property-Based Falsification', 'Adversarial End-to-End Simulation', 'Executable Reference Model', and
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-F2 (CRITICAL): despite five step titles explicitly claiming to build and run executable/simulation models, the 270-step, 550-file numbered corpus contains ZERO actual executable artifacts — each such step contains only prose narrating what a hypothetical program would report; the only genuine Python files anywhere in the corpus were written by a separate, later review session (not the step-corpus itself) and cover only three specific claims out of several hundred made across the programme — directly explaining why the corpus could never run its own nominated strongest empirical test (EV-A1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: None of these findings is a claim that the corpus is dishonest. ARCs A, D and E in particular contain mathematics of real quality, and Steps 240, 255, 260, 266 and 267 state their own negative results plainly. The findings are about what the corpus's method could not reach: it could not execute, and
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing methodological caveat: none of the EV findings allege dishonesty — several arcs (A, D, E) contain genuinely high-quality mathematics, and the corpus itself plainly states several of its own negative results (Steps 240, 255, 260, 266, 267); the findings instead characterize a structural limit of the corpus's method — it could never execute code, and after step 258 it could no longer check itself against a genuinely independent second source.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Purpose: produce EXECUTED evidence where the corpus has only PROSE. Nothing here is architecture. Nothing here is authoritative. It is a witness. The kernel implements the corpus's TERMINAL formal model, taken from Steps 262/263/265/267/269.
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel's stated purpose is explicitly to produce EXECUTED evidence where the corpus itself has only prose, and it explicitly disclaims any authoritative or architectural status for itself, calling itself merely 'a witness' — directly operationalizing the theory-evolution-map's EV-F2 critique that the numbered-step corpus never actually runs code.

b_rows_sample.statement: Final conclusion of the executable experiment set: H3 (K=(A,R) is a sufficient history abstraction) is left UNDECIDED and H4 (this session's EV-E1 claim) is CONFIRMED by execution — K=(A,R)'s sufficiency holds if and only if the mandatory operation set excludes every history-sensitive predicate, and since the corpus never actually closes that operation set (Step 266 leaves the operation registry incomplete and policy/authority non-computable as specified), the widely-repeated claim 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient state' is explicitly judged NOT a theorem of the corpus but merely a consequence of an unstated choice of the operation set O.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every D285 hypothesis must be typed before it can be tested. In particular, an equality-dependent hypothesis must explicitly state which equality relation it uses. Otherwise a formally correct-looking proposition may be mathematically vacuous. ... This is the single most important methodological correction to emerge from the entire Gītā-KnowledgeOS integration effort.
a_rows_sample.statement: States and elevates the typing/equality-naming requirement to the status of the single most important methodological finding of the entire Gita-integration effort, generalizing beyond the single artifact (D285-5) where it was first observed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1 Source proposition; 2 KnowledgeOS translation (do not assume correspondence valid merely because terms sound similar); 3 Formal hypothesis; 4 Type/equality audit (structural/semantic/observational/identity/other; check non-vacuity); 5 Independent KnowledgeOS derivation (would KOS require this even if the Gītā had never been consulted?); 6 Executable/falsifiable test; 7 Classification (mathematical/architectural/DDD/philosophical analogy/Gītā corroboration/unresolved hypothesis/governance decision).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the finalized seven-stage D285-x protocol in full, most notably promoting the independence question (stage 5) to a mandatory, distinct pipeline stage rather than an optional afterthought, and expanding the classification stage to seven explicit categories.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equality Specification: NONE REQUIRED — and stating that is part of the discipline. The Θ rejection is a type-checking result (four carriers), not an equality claim. Asserting an equality here would be a category error.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates correct application of the frozen seven-stage protocol's type/equality-audit stage by explicitly recording that no equality relation applies to this particular result (it is a type-checking failure, not an equality claim) -- itself a disciplined act, since asserting an unnecessary equality specification would itself be a category error under the same protocol.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is an exemplary artifact. It demonstrates exactly the methodological discipline that Steps 285-286 require. ... The artifact is accepted as written and should serve as the template for all D285-x tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a full acceptance verdict for the D285-5 action/result formal test (t285_reconcile.py's T-E, S2063), the only unconditionally-accepted artifact identified across this batch's entire Step 285/286 research thread, and designates it the template for all subsequent D285-x work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Required Structure: 1 Property Statement; 2 Trivial vs Substantive; 3 Execution; 4 Qualification; 5 Equality Specification; 6 Independence; 7 Classification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the mandatory 7-section template every future D285-x formal-test artifact must follow, generalized from the structure of the accepted D285-5 artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Next Steps: 1 Adopt this artifact as template for D285-x; 2 Execute remaining D285-x tests using this format; 3 Ensure each test specifies its equality relation; 4 Document independence for each property; 5 Classify each property using R0-RX.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues five forward-looking directives operationalizing the acceptance verdict, most notably requiring every future test to explicitly specify its equality relation -- directly anticipating (and setting up) the self-critical re-examination of the reviewer's own prior K-projection claim carried out in the companion script t285_equality.py (S2072).

b_rows_sample.anchor: **A hypothesis cannot be tested until its types and equality relation are explicit.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest methodological result as: a hypothesis cannot be tested until its types and equality relation are explicit; frames the seven-stage protocol (source proposition -> KOS translation -> formal hypothesis -> type/equality audit -> independent KOS derivation -> falsifiable test -> classification) plus the seven-section D285 artifact template as the resulting stronger research discipline, and states the four equality relations must be treated as non-interchangeable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### 5 · Equality Specification ⭐ **NONE REQUIRED** — no equality is asserted. The matrix relates *candidates to consequences*, which is an implication, not an identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the mandated 7-part D285-x template to itself and explicitly notes an edge case: this artifact requires NO equality specification, since it relates candidates to consequences (an implication) rather than asserting any identity between two things — distinguishing 'implication' from 'identity' as a template category.

Note: The finalized, HPA-accepted seven-stage protocol required for every future D285-x artifact: (1) Source proposition -- exact Gita chapter/verse, textual claim vs interpretation; (2) KnowledgeOS translation -- never assume validity merely because terms sound similar; (3) Formal hypothesis -- mathematical or DDD statement; (4) Type/equality audit -- name the specific equality relation and check non-vacuity; (5) Independent KnowledgeOS derivation -- would KOS require this without the Gita; (6) Executable/falsifiable test -- concrete positive/negative cases; (7) Classification -- separate mathematical/architectural/DDD/philosophical-analogy/Gita-corroboration/unresolved/governance results. a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in a form that is comprehensible, actionable, and faithful to the underlying epistemic structure, enabling the Knower to make an informed decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Q24 definition (later corrected): a decision-ready state IS the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in comprehensible, actionable, faithful form. Key boxed claims: Presentation ≠ Dump of Raw Data; Presentation = Structured, Epistemically Qualified, Purpose-Tailored View; Presentation must preserve the epistemic status of each assertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P_t = \text{Present}(K_t, I_t, U_t, \Delta_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, \text{Format})
a_rows_sample.statement: The Presentation Function: Present maps (K,I,U,Δ,Q,C,N,F) to a presentation P_t; nine presentation components listed (State Summary, Key Findings, Gaps and Conflicts, Ideal Comparison, Risks and Implications, Recommendations, Epistemic Status, Provenance, History); five presentation layers (Executive Summary, Epistemic State, Comparison with Ideal, Risks and Implications, Recommendations), each with purpose/content/format.

type_signature.domain: K x I x U x Δ x Q x C x N x Format

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision Context:\n   "You are deciding whether to participate in the battle."
a_rows_sample.statement: Presentation formats illustrated with the Arjuna case: Natural Language Summary, Structured View (assertion/status/evidence/conflict table), Visual View (graph with a conflict warning), and Comparative View (dimension/current/ideal/gap table); repeated in section 8 as 'The Arjuna Example: Presentation' with an executive summary, epistemic state view and comparative view.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Very Strong** | Very High Confidence | 🟢 |
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic status indicator vocabularies for UI: Confidence Indicators (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None with colors), Conflict Indicators (None/Potential/Active/Resolved), Gap Indicators (Missing Dimension/Unknown Value/Missing Evidence/Stale Knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q(P_t) = w_F \cdot \text{Fidelity} + w_C \cdot \text{Comprehensibility} + w_A \cdot \text{Actionability} + w_M \cdot \text{Completeness}
a_rows_sample.statement: Original presentation quality criteria (Fidelity, Comprehensibility, Actionability, Completeness, each in [0,1]) combined into a single weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t); four original invariants: Presentation ≠ Raw Data; must preserve epistemic status; must be comprehensible; must be actionable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original document's closing claim, later retracted: a 24-item list of the 'complete KnowledgeOS model' (Observation, Dimension, Proposition, Assertion, Evidence, Epistemic State, Knowledge State, Understanding State, Domain State, Ideal State, Coherence, Conflict, Gap, Distance, Zero/Lord/Sārathi Lens, Transition, History, Complete System State, Discrepancy, Prioritization, Decision-Ready State, Presentation) is declared 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_t \xrightarrow{\text{evaluate}} D_t \xrightarrow{\text{project}} P_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Fundamental correction: presentation must not become part of the epistemic state itself; it is a projection for a Knower/purpose/decision/format. Pipeline corrected to S_t --evaluate--> D_t --project--> P_t, where S_t is the complete internal state, D_t the decision-ready assessment/posture, P_t the human-facing projection. Establishes P_t ≠ D_t and P_t ≠ S_t: presentation is a view/projection, not another knowledge object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation = Epistemically\ Qualified\ Projection
a_rows_sample.statement: Deeper DDD point: Present() must not be understood as 'turn database objects into UI' but as a semantic projection that decides what is relevant, critical, uncertain, conflicting, missing, evidenced, recommendation-vs-fact, and inference-vs-observation. Presentation = Epistemically Qualified Projection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \Pi_{N,D,P,C,F}
a_rows_sample.statement: New concept: Presentation Projection Π_{N,D,P,C,F} parameterized by Knower N, Decision D, Purpose P, Context C, Format F, giving P_t = Π_{N,D,P,C,F}(S_t). Enables two different Knowers to receive different presentations of the same underlying state without KnowledgeOS holding two different Knowledge States.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the original weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t) as formal theory because it again permits compensation: a presentation could score 95% comprehensibility/actionability/completeness while misrepresenting one critical epistemic status, and still get a high score — unacceptable. Replaces with hard presentation invariants: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required, CriticalEpistemicStatusPreserved(P_t,S_t), DecisionRelevantInformationPreserved(P_t,D); optional metrics may still assess quality afterward.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CompleteForDecision(P_t,D)
a_rows_sample.statement: Completeness should be formalized as decision-relative, CompleteForDecision(P_t,D), not generic Complete(P_t), since a presentation can deliberately omit decision-irrelevant information; expressed generally as Relevance = f(Knower, Purpose, Decision, Context).

a_rows_sample.statement: Keeps the five presentation layers but re-semanticizes them: Layer 1 Decision (what decision is supported), Layer 2 Evidence/Knowledge (what do we know), Layer 3 Epistemic qualification (how do we know it), Layer 4 Discrepancy/Risk (what remains uncertain/problematic), Layer 5 Guidance (what should the Knower consider next) — giving the progression Decision→Knowledge→Evidence→Discrepancy→Action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CurrentState \neq History
a_rows_sample.statement: History should not be dumped into the main presentation but disclosed progressively: primary view answers 'what is the state now?', user can expand to 'how did we arrive here?'. CurrentState ≠ History, but History -> ExplanationOfCurrentState.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
KnowledgeOS Core

Owns:

K,\Sigma,E,G,C,\Delta,I,S
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces three bounded responsibilities/contexts: KnowledgeOS Core (owns K,Σ,E,G,C,Δ,I,S), Epistemic Orchestration (owns Zero, Lord, Sārathi, Prioritization, Transition), and Presentation/Interaction (owns Projection, View, Format, Explanation, Interaction), with a layered diagram Core -> Epistemic Assessment -> Decision State -> Presentation Projection -> (Executive/Detailed/Graph views).

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy)
a_rows_sample.statement: Revised mathematical model: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy); P_t = Π(S_t,D_t,N,F); with P_t ≢ S_t and P_t ≢ D_t, and P_t defined as 'human-oriented projection of S_t under D_t'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation \neq RawData
a_rows_sample.statement: Nine new presentation invariants recommended to be frozen: Presentation ≠ RawData; Presentation ≠ KnowledgeState; Presentation ≠ Decision; Recommendation ≠ Fact; Candidate ≠ Knowledge; Presentation must preserve critical epistemic distinctions; Presentation must preserve provenance for decision-relevant claims; Presentation completeness is decision-relative; Presentation is a projection, not a mutation of the Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ConceptualCompleteness \neq FormalCompleteness
a_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the original document's closing claim that the 24-question model is 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'; proposes calling it instead 'KnowledgeOS Epistemic Model — Conceptual and Formal Specification', listing items still needing formalization: exact ontology/type system, proposition semantics, evidence model, inference semantics, conflict algebra, gap detection semantics, Ideal State construction, discrepancy semantics, decision criteria, transition semantics, authorization/governance, persistence semantics, concurrency/versioning, presentation projection semantics. States ConceptualCompleteness ≠ FormalCompleteness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the opposite of belief is not necessarily disbelief; the proper opposite can be conscious ignorance or doubt. Deliberate doubt can amount to a 'not proven' verdict because the evidence does not determine either side. ... NOT_PROVEN != REJECTED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Whately's doubt-is-not-disbelief distinction motivates preserving BELIEF/DISBELIEF/DOUBT/IGNORANCE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as potentially distinct states and adding a NOT_PROVEN state distinct from REJECTED to the epistemic-state model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD says we should separate dimensions. ... Claim: EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition. ... Otherwise we create a combinatorial state machine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-correction of the previously proposed single combined epistemic-state list into four independent Claim-attached dimensions (EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition), avoiding a combinatorial single state machine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN does not necessarily mean: Nobody knows. It can mean: The current inquiry has not established an epistemically sufficient standing for this proposition. ... UNKNOWN_TO_US while KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines UNKNOWN to mean 'the current inquiry has not established sufficient epistemic standing', distinct from 'nobody knows'; proposes UNKNOWN_TO_US as compatible with KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B, connecting back to Russell's acquaintance/description distinction and Davidson on interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Support \neq Probability
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the earlier Q16 correction (Support ≠ Truth, Support ≠ Resolution) with Support ≠ Probability unless a probabilistic model is explicitly defined — 'Strong evidence' does not mathematically mean P(True)=0.95 unless the system has actually defined that probability semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UncertaintyType \neq UncertaintyMagnitude
b_rows_sample.statement: Uncertainty vocabulary (None/Low/Moderate/High/VeryHigh) is acceptable as a policy vocabulary but not yet a mathematical quantity — the theory has not decided whether uncertainty means lack of information, ambiguity, variance between sources, probability, confidence, or epistemic indeterminacy; flags UncertaintyType ≠ UncertaintyMagnitude as a future question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: StrongSupport \not\Rightarrow Current
b_rows_sample.statement: Validity should be separated into TemporalValidity(A,t) and EpistemicStatus(A): a fact can be strongly supported but temporally expired, so StrongSupport ⇏ Current.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = (Source,\ Content,\ Relevance,\ Reliability,\ Time,\ Provenance)
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence needs its own model rather than being just 'E': Evidence = (Source, Content, Relevance, Reliability, Time, Provenance), plus an EvidenceRelation(A,E) since evidence may support, weaken, contradict, qualify, or contextualize an assertion. Establishes Evidence ≠ Support — Support is a relation/assessment between evidence and assertion, called 'a significant missing DDD object'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HierarchyOfFaculties \neq EpistemicConfidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 3 (verses 40, 43) orders Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self as distinct faculties, tempting an 'epistemic ladder' reading; explicitly rejects that reading (reaffirming the earlier rejection of Unknown<Observed<Confirmed<Resolved as a universal ladder): HierarchyOfFaculties ≠ EpistemicConfidence — the text describes different faculties/levels of operation, not better evidence. Abstracts a non-theological CognitiveCapability = {Perception, Interpretation, Reasoning, Judgment, Orientation}, explicitly kept out of Σ_A and placed in the actor/agent model instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge \neq Understanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Called 'perhaps the most important validation of the entire KnowledgeOS concept': a person can act on FalseInterpretation while possessing many correct facts (Arjuna's opening situation), giving Knowledge ≠ Understanding and CorrectFacts ⇏ CorrectDecision. Formally defines Understanding U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty): Knowledge = 'what is represented', Understanding = 'what does it mean, imply and require in this context'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Understanding = Interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms K≠U (Knowledge ≠ Understanding, validated by Arjuna's opening bewilderment despite already having heard distinctions) but corrects the previous U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty) tuple as too implementation-oriented; redefines Understanding as 'interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context', from which implications, consequences, applicability and normative significance are derived facets.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā hierarchy \neq KnowledgeOS epistemic hierarchy
b_rows_sample.statement: Names 'perhaps the most important correction': the Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self hierarchy (verses 40,43) is a metaphysical faculty hierarchy from the source, not evidence for an Observation<Interpretation<Reasoning<Truth epistemic-confidence ladder — that would be 'our invention, not the text'. Similarly the smoke/dust/embryo covering analogy should not become a software confidence scale; the only legitimate architectural extraction is 'AccessToKnowledgeCanBeObscuredToDifferentDegrees', with the exact ontology left to the source's own philosophical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Information 
eq Evidence 
eq Belief 
eq Knowledge 
eq Understanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Endorses the book's knowledge/understanding distinction (understanding requires coherent explanatory grasp) and extends the research lattice to a five-term chain Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Belief ≠ Knowledge ≠ Understanding, explicitly flagged as 'a research distinction, not yet a Core object model'. Evaluates the book summary's proposed relation set (observes, measures, knows, understands, complements, constitutes, limits) one by one, rejecting 'constitutes(measurement,knowledge)' as too theory-laden to become a Kernel relation until measurement is shown universally necessary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U_{sem}\neq U_{epi}\neq U_{dom}
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects InterpretationConfidence=EpistemicSupport (an LLM can be extremely confident in an incorrect interpretation) and introduces three distinct uncertainties: Semantic uncertainty U_sem (what does the source mean?), Epistemic uncertainty U_epi (how well supported is the proposition?), Domain uncertainty U_dom (what is actually true in the domain?) — U_sem≠U_epi≠U_dom, 'a significant strengthening of our earlier four-dimensional epistemic model'. Also states Ambiguity ≠ Error: multiple candidate meanings (e.g. 'Nexus is running' as OperationalStatus/Process/NexusService running) should be preserved until context resolves them — ambiguity is itself a valid epistemic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown ... Hypothesized ... Reported ... WeaklySupported ... ModeratelySupported ... StronglySupported ... Confirmed ... Conflicting ... Stale ... Invalidated ... Absent
b_rows_sample.statement: Expands the epistemic state space Σ into an eleven-value enumeration with worked examples: Unknown (dimension exists, value unknown), Hypothesized (candidate proposed, unevaluated), Reported (source reported, unverified), WeaklySupported, ModeratelySupported, StronglySupported, Confirmed (verified via multiple independent sources), Conflicting (multiple sources disagree), Stale (once known, may no longer be current), Invalidated (believed then disproven), Absent (determined not to exist). Defines the Admission Boundary formally: Admit:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->Assertion, explicitly NOT requiring StronglySupported, Confirmed, or Truth — 'admission means this proposition is now part of the Knowledge State, with an explicit epistemic status', a much lower and more defensible boundary than a truth-threshold.

type_signature.domain: candidate assertion x evidence x rules x context

b_rows_sample.anchor: Support = f(E,\Pi,C,\mathcal R)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects Support=|E| (evidence count) since evidence differs in relevance, reliability, independence, freshness, provenance, directness, context: Support=f(E,Π,C,R). Requires an explicit evidence-dependency graph to detect non-independent evidence — e.g. if Document->LLM (the LLM derived its answer from the document), the LLM's output is not independent evidence even though it appears as a fourth source alongside DB/Monitoring/Document — 'evidence independence must be explicitly modelled', flagged as important for Zero.

Evidence ≠ EvidenceQuality: even a poor-quality observation-proposition pair can be an evidence relation; quality is evaluated separately as a 7-dimensional vector Q_E=(Reliability,Relevance,Directness,Independence,Freshness,Reproducibility,ProvenanceQuality) rather than a single confidence number — 'much more faithful than confidence=0.87'. EvidenceType≠EvidenceStrength (a direct measurement can be wrong; a mathematical derivation can be extremely strong; an official document can be stale), and EvidenceQuality=f(E,P,C,R) since e.g. a direct runtime observation may dominate for 'what is running now?' while an official architecture document may dominate for 'what was officially approved?' — no universal ranking exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 \succeq_{P,C,R} E_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a universal total ordering E_1>E_2 in favor of a partial comparison E_1≽_{P,C,R}E_2 ('under proposition P, context C and rule R, E_1 is at least as suitable as E_2'), since evidence can be genuinely incomparable (e.g. a direct runtime measurement vs an official governance decision). Evidence quality vectors are compared via a policy ComparisonRule(P,C)->Ordering rather than collapsed to a scalar average (e.g. Q(E_1)=(0.95,0.98,1.0,...) is NOT reduced to Q(E)=0.94) — different policies weight different dimensions (directness/freshness for runtime state; authority/provenance for governance compliance).

type_signature.domain: evidence pairs x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reliability(E) = f(Source, ObservationMethod, Environment, Configuration, Context, Provenance)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Reliability from a property of the source alone to Reliability=f(Source,ObservationMethod,Environment,Configuration,Context,Provenance): even an 'official Nexus database' can produce an unreliable observation if queried against the wrong environment, a stale replica, or a broken synchronization. Corrects Completeness similarly to be proposition-relative — Completeness(E,P,C,ρ), not Completeness(E) — since a version field alone may be complete for 'what is the version?' but radically incomplete for 'is Nexus ready for migration?'.

b_aliases: separate dimensions, not one combinatorial state machine

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the robot is not the core domain. The robot is a consumer and operator of governed knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the constitutional boundary for the proposed Digitalization Robot: it consumes and operates on governed knowledge, but never becomes the core domain or an independent authority source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mode 1: Advisor ... Mode 2: Developer Assistant ... Mode 3: Controlled Executor ... Mode 4: Autonomous Operator
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four graduated robot authority modes with increasing execution permission (from recommend-only to fully autonomous in limited domains), explicitly refusing to assume the robot always executes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: skill: name: Create REST API requires: [...] produces: [...] evidence: required
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a governed 'Robot Skill Catalog' where each skill declares its required inputs, produced artifacts, and mandatory evidence, and that the Composition Root injects interchangeable tool adapters (e.g. Kubernetes vs AWS vs Azure) behind each skill.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The robot does not only produce software. It increases the intelligence of the organization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the strategic differentiator versus current AI coding agents is a closing feedback loop: the robot's work produces new organizational knowledge (an evidence package) that KnowledgeOS stores, rather than terminating at code output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Command → Application Boundary → Aggregate → Domain Rule → Domain Event ... no actor may 'Change Governance.' directly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the proposed governed command loop as the integration spine any actor (human, AI agent, or the Digitalization Robot) must issue commands through, with outcomes surfacing only as domain events, never a direct write to Governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel can become the part of the future brain that guarantees that whatever the brain claims to know has an accountable, identifiable, justified and historically preserved epistemic state. ... The possibility of becoming part of a future computer brain must never be used to enlarge the present Kernel boundary. Build the smallest correct epistemic core now.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a future-facing hypothesis that today's narrow KnowledgeOS Core could become the epistemic-integrity substrate of a much larger future cognitive system (perception/interpretation/reasoning/planning/action wrapped around it), while explicitly constraining that this future possibility must never be used to enlarge the present Kernel boundary -- the smallest correct epistemic core must be built now, regardless of future ambition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

b_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
b_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Agent-001: Every knowledge state SHALL be constitutionally coupled to the epistemic agent (Knower) that asserted, observed, or reasoned it. The agent's identity, role, and epistemic capacity are preserved as protected dimensions of the knowledge object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a first version of the Knower invariant: every knowledge state must be constitutionally coupled to the epistemic agent that produced it, so that 'who knows' remains inseparable from 'what is known'; framed as completing the Tripuṭī (Knower-Knowing-Known) trinity and as the engineering translation of the Gita's Kṣetrajña.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel should not bind knowledge to a person permanently. It should preserve the epistemic origin and agency relationship... Knowledge = traceable through knowers, observers, reasoners, and authorities.
a_rows_sample.statement: Self-corrects H-KOS-Agent-001's 'inseparable ownership' framing: knowledge is not owned by a knower, it is traceable through knowers/observers/reasoners/authorities; a knowledge object may survive the disappearance of its original observer, but its epistemic lineage must survive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Agent-001 (Candidate): KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the epistemic agency associated with every knowledge state, including who observed, who interpreted, who reasoned, who validated, and under which authority context the knowledge state was produced.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refined, 'stronger and more general' successor to H-KOS-Agent-001: preserves epistemic agency (observer/reasoner/validator/authority-context) rather than binding knowledge to a single knower's identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ज्ञाता (Jñātā) — Knower | ज्ञान (Jñāna) — Knowing | ज्ञेय (Jñeya) — Known ... Knowledge without epistemic origin loses accountability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the Vedanta Tripuṭī (Jñātā/Jñāna/Jñeya) onto KnowledgeOS interpretation (Epistemic Agent / Reasoning-transformation process / Knowledge object-proposition); the engineering extraction is not metaphysical truth but that knowledge without epistemic origin loses accountability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Opening — the Knower as owner
a_rows_sample.statement: States the formal model begins with an owner: the Knower owns the problem, the purpose, the IdealState, and final authority — invariant I-1, the only invariant that survived three entire methodological regimes of the discovery corpus unchanged; whatever else was torn down and rebuilt, ownership of the frame never moved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Convergence with the repository side
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Knower is the one concept found on both sides of the programme under the same lineage — the formal model's Knower (I-1) and the repository constitution's protected first-class epistemic agent (H-KOS-Agent-001, 'the Knower of the Field') — with the convergence PARTIAL: both make the Knower constitutive and inseparable, but ownership of goal and IdealState is established only on the formal side.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant I-11 closes the I-1 hole
a_rows_sample.statement: I-11: no in-force policy -- the AcceptancePolicy and the constitution included -- changes without a governed, versioned approval decision; self-modification of the in-force policy is excluded by construction, not by exhortation. I-11 closes the hole the falsification pass found in I-1: the Knower's ownership now reaches Determination through the governed policy chain instead of stopping short at an unowned policy object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Sarathi reading hardens into I-1
a_rows_sample.statement: After the crisis, the corpus reorganized itself around numbered questions -- how does knowledge change state, who owns the goal, what makes evidence sufficient -- and, in parallel, returned to the Gita lens with new seriousness. The era's great gift to the final architecture is the Sarathi (charioteer) reading: the Knower owns the frame; everything else serves it. Of all the era's images, this is the one that hardened into an invariant (I-1) and survived every later regime unchanged. When Part III.2 says the Knower owns problem, purpose, IdealState, and final authority, it is speaking the formalized residue of this reading.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NEITHER, precisely: the corpus contains the RELATIONS but not their DECISION PROCEDURES. Four relations are named and declared non-interchangeable — so equality is not a missing primitive. But three of the four cannot be evaluated: ≡ has no procedure, ≈ has no observation set, ≅_λ has no definition of 'relevant'. Equality is an under-specified corpus primitive, not an absent one — the same shape as Qualify, and the same class of gap (G1).
a_rows_sample.statement: Delivers the definitive answer to Reviewer B's central research question, generalizing beyond equality itself: identifies a recurring structural pattern across the whole Step-285/286 programme where the corpus names a construct and declares its type/role, but omits the decision procedure or computational body needed to actually evaluate it -- explicitly unifying this equality finding with the earlier Qualify-function gap (S2063/S2068, the (W,Ω)/K-projection computability blocker) as instances of the same underlying gap class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What would close it: a decision on 254 Decision 3 (is Π inside ≡?) and a declared permitted-observation set for ≈. Both are NORMATIVE. Neither is taken here.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the exact two normative (governance) decisions that would resolve the equality under-specification -- ratifying Decision 3 (whether provenance is part of semantic equality) and declaring a permitted-observation set for observational equality -- and explicitly declines to make either decision within this research pass, correctly leaving them for governance.
