World
\neq
Observation
\neq
Evidence
\neq
Interpretation
\neq
EpistemicState
\neq
Evaluation
\neq
KnowledgeAttribution.
$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to preserve a seven-layer non-collapse chain (World≠Observation≠Evidence≠Interpretation≠EpistemicState≠Evaluation≠KnowledgeAttribution) and forbids giving the simulated agent access to hidden ground truth: Contr(p,Kt) must not mean 'the world makes both p and not-p true' but that the epistemic representation simultaneously contains incompatible commitments about p.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## Candidate A — Fourth value ... ## 6. CANDIDATE B — Delegate contradiction to consistency ... # 7. CANDIDATE C — Exclusive construction ... # 8. CANDIDATE D — STRUCTURED EVALUATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the four candidate representations to test fairly: A) extend {T,F,U} to {T,F,U,C}, testing whether C is primitive/derivable/needs provenance or polarity/can coexist with U; B) keep Sat in {T,F,U} and represent Contr(p,K) as an independent relation outside Sat; C) exclusive-by-construction (bot ≡ not-p∈K ∧ p∉K), explicitly flagged as expected-vulnerable to silently converting contradictory into false/absent/invalid; D) a structured EVal=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,polarity) tuple whose exact fields must be discovered by reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\forall (x,y)\in\mathcal R_{req},
\quad
x\neq y
\Rightarrow
R(x)\neq R(y).
$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy for this experiment: a candidate representation R:S->D is adequate iff for every required distinction pair (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); a structured representation may satisfy this even when two conditions share the same primary 'value' field, so uniqueness of the primary value is not required.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Case 1 — Unknown ... ### Case 15 — Model conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 15-case deterministic adversarial suite: unknown, absent, not-assessed, insufficient evidence, underdetermined, unobservable, direct contradiction, conflicting sources, conflicting observations, unequal-confidence contradiction, retraction, supersession, different contexts, different times, and model conflict -- each with an expected semantic condition and an instruction not to prejudge borderline cases (e.g. source conflict vs epistemic contradiction, retraction should not automatically create contradiction).

a_rows_sample.statement: Pre-registers eight candidate negative results to actively search for (NEG-1..8): a fourth value C cannot distinguish contradiction subtypes; structured evaluation still collapses required distinctions; contradiction is context-dependent and cannot be represented without context; contradiction is temporal and cannot be represented statically; source conflict is not epistemic contradiction; contradiction cannot be reduced to Sat; Zero cannot be determined from contradiction alone; a supposedly minimal representation loses provenance or temporal distinctions.

b_rows_sample.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: don't turn every fundamental concept into an aggregate of lower-level constructs · don't derive the ontology from the representation format · don't solve a primitive concept by renaming it
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F037 proposes three modelling prohibitions as the corpus's self-diagnosis: (1) don't turn every fundamental concept into an aggregate of lower-level constructs -- names what produced an earlier god-aggregate and its four member lists; (2) don't derive the ontology from the representation format -- restates an existing inference rule (S1-F027) at modelling time, of which an indexed case (<C-1>) is an instance; (3) don't solve a primitive concept by renaming it -- names a four-name pattern directly (KnowledgeClaim -> KnowledgeElement -> 'identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record' -> Assertion; workbook item PS-1, still unmerged). The reviewer confirms Session 1's mapping as sound, and notes prohibition 3 sharpens a sibling review's verdict (S2-R-F036) by making explicit whether 'assertion record' is a fifth name for one unresolved primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Seven results survive with their reasoning intact. ... **And a second class that survives as instruments rather than findings — seventeen of them** ... **Five of them have never been run.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven substantive results survive independent review with their reasoning intact: the anti-reasoner constraint (S1-F025, mechanism-independent and decidable regardless of which member list wins, supplying the argument for an existing prohibition law only asserted); store-the-substrate/compute-the-measure (S1-F038/F040, law-consistent and independently justified by Roberts' homomorphism condition); the minimum preservation unit (S1-F036, survives the atomicity falsification untouched); atomicity-not-relatedness (S1-F016, conclusion survives an adversarial commission built to break it, though its 'six arrivals' justification does not); the finite/unbounded minimality argument (S1-F039, the only technical, non-assertive ground for Kernel minimality in the corpus); the three modelling prohibitions (S1-F037, the corpus's own diagnosis of how it went wrong); and measure theory refused as ontology (S1-F040, the only complete propose-refute-resolve cycle in the corpus, six refutations at four levels resolved in 78 minutes). A second class survives as seventeen instruments whose function is to prevent implementation (separation rule, corrected preserve/perform asymmetry, twelve-question sequence, relatedness-vs-atomicity test, conditional exclusions, consumption rule, falsification routing, Tarka families, decidability test, counterfactual robustness, removal test, the three prohibitions, measurement-as-homomorphism, acceptance tests), of which five have never actually been run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The research supports a **narrow and unglamorous** answer. What such a system must be able to do is **reconstruct**: *"this assertion was evaluated as X, under regime R, in context C, at time T, on evidence E"* ... **Seven genera stand unreconciled.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Answering whether KnowledgeOS could be 'the brain of a computer' from surviving evidence, not the raw tally: the research supports a narrow, unglamorous answer -- such a system must be able to reconstruct ('this assertion was evaluated as X, under regime R, in context C, at time T, on evidence E'), not determine truth (an existing law refuses a truth oracle) and not reason (an existing law forbids it, with the anti-reasoner constraint supplying the reason: a boundary that reconstructs interpretation in order to decide admission would be circular). Three surviving results converge on this shape, none about intelligence: preserve-structures-perform-reasoning-elsewhere (with a technical minimality argument); store-the-substrate-compute-the-measure (no stored scores, no assumed metric, no global continuity); and the minimum preservation unit (an identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record). One honest negative is recorded: the corpus asked 'what is knowledge itself?' on its final research day, after ~160 documents, and closed the definitional programme in the negative -- seven genera of knowledge stand unreconciled. A 'brain' whose central term is undefined is not thereby impossible, but the research does not supply the definition, and says so itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The smallest thing KnowledgeOS must preserve is an identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record. ... What exactly is the identity-bearing thing? ... preservation unit vs consistency boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the corpus's most precise answer to 'what must be preserved': an identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record — immediately self-qualified with 'what exactly is the identity-bearing thing?' — and deliberately separates the preservation-unit question from the consistency-boundary (atomicity) question, a distinction the corpus elsewhere merges; three roles (preservation unit / consistency boundary / projection view) are separated here where the corpus elsewhere conflates them, dissolving part of an earlier F016↔F019 dispute where one side attacked consistency and the other defended preservation while both used the word 'aggregate'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion is a Kernel primitive. ... Assertion is probably not fundamental. ... Both sentences are in the same document. ... a thing deserves fundamental status when removing it loses a non-redundant capability ... I record it as a contradiction the source leaves standing, with the reconciliation marked as my inference and not adopted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records an intra-document contradiction: the same source document asserts both 'Assertion is a Kernel primitive' and 'Assertion is probably not fundamental'; offers, but explicitly does not adopt, a possible reconciliation via Merricks' non-redundancy criterion (Assertion could be the right Kernel primitive — what the Kernel operates on — without being ontologically fundamental/irreducible); this is the corpus's first explicit ontological-reduction test applied to its own vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.statement: Extends successor-state semantics to concurrent action sets (successor-state axiom for a concurrent-action fluent), and identifies the 'precondition interaction problem': individually-possible concurrent actions (startMoveLeft, startMoveRight) can be jointly impossible even though each satisfies its own precondition axiom, requiring additional interaction constraints beyond the individual precondition axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [EXT] throughout. Extracted, not endorsed. ... The induction axiom is second-order. The extraction states the consequence plainly: the system is not fully first-order decidable. Any transfer inherits this. ... It rests on the causal completeness assumption ... This is an assumption about the axiomatiser's knowledge, not a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Reiter's formal ontology and axioms (already captured in S2536) under an explicit [EXT]/'extracted not endorsed' framing, emphasizing two carried-forward limitations for any KnowledgeOS transfer: the induction axiom is second-order (not fully first-order decidable), and the successor-state axiom rests on an unproven causal-completeness ASSUMPTION about the axiomatiser's own knowledge, not a theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "conflicting_effects_from_F_false": ["F"], "conflicting_effects_from_F_true": ["F"], "conflict_resolved_silently_in_favour_of_gamma_plus": true, "finding": "when gamma+ and gamma- both name F, the SSA yields F TRUE with no signal that the effect axioms were inconsistent. The frame solution PRESUPPOSES consistent effect axioms; it does not detect their inconsistency."
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed result: a deliberately conflicting action (gamma+ and gamma- both naming fluent F) is silently resolved to F=TRUE from both prior states, with the successor-state axiom giving no signal that its own effect axioms were inconsistent -- confirming determinism and persistence-of-unmentioned-fluents work correctly, but exposing that inconsistency detection is entirely outside the mechanism's scope.

NOT a state.""" ... def successor(self, a, state): """Successor state axiom:  F' = gamma+ ∨ (F ∧ ¬gamma-)""" ... def regress(self, fluent, sit): """REGRESSION: rewrite a query about sit into a query about S0, by unwinding the successor-state axiom backwards."""
b_rows_sample.statement: A minimal but faithful executable model of Reiter's situation calculus: a Situation as an immutable action tuple (explicitly a history, not a state), an ActionTheory with Poss/successor(SSA)/progress/executable/regress methods, used to generate all five A1-A5 experimental results in this batch; module docstring explicitly frames these as verification tests of Reiter's machinery, not a KnowledgeOS implementation, and states nothing here promotes any Reiter concept to a KnowledgeOS primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
a_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
a_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

Verdict: History(K)!=K is fundamental; lambda belongs outside K as History:K->Histories, mathematically verified, and aligned with the real implementation (a separate lineage graph, no KnowledgeState).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We want to know whether there exists a corresponding state transformation T:K x I -> K such that F(That(H,i)) = T(F(H),i) for every valid H and input i. If this holds, then the history dynamics descend to the state space.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the formal question of state sufficiency: given a history space H, a proposed state abstraction F:H->K, and a history-level transformation That:HxI->H, does a corresponding state-level transformation T:KxI->K exist such that F(That(H,i))=T(F(H),i) for all valid H,i -- i.e. do history dynamics descend to the state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_A ~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B). Then state sufficiency requires: H_A ~_F H_B => That(H_A,i) ~_F That(H_B,i). Thus ~_F must be a congruence with respect to valid transformations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the equivalence relation ~_F induced by the state abstraction (H_A~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B)) and states the central congruence requirement: this equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation for the state representation to be sufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now suppose the proposed state representation retains only Content(K)={p}. ... Authorized(A)=true but Authorized(B)=false. Then F(That(H_A,validate)) != F(That(H_B,validate)). Yet initially F(H_A)=F(H_B). Content-only K fails the congruence test. This is a genuine falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a content-only knowledge state via a worked example: two histories with different evidence sources (A authorized, B not) collapse to the same content-only state, but a governance-sensitive validation transformation produces divergent outcomes (Validated vs Unvalidated) depending on the discarded source information -- a genuine congruence failure, showing content-only K is insufficient once authority-sensitive transformations are valid operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we enrich the state with lambda(e)=source(e). Now F(H_A) != F(H_B) ... The previous counterexample disappears. But this does not yet prove sufficiency. We have only shown one missing distinction has been restored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows adding a source/provenance field lambda(e)=source(e) to the state resolves the specific counterexample found, but explicitly cautions this only restores one missing distinction and does not establish global sufficiency -- more collapsed-but-behaviorally-different histories must still be searched for.

F(H_C)=F(H_D) under a representation that omits policy history. But T(H_C,i) != T(H_D,i). ... Is Policy part of state, provenance, or external context? ... It is de
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a further counterexample: two histories identical in content and provenance but produced under different policies collapse to the same state under a policy-omitting representation, yet future validation depending on the original governing policy produces different results -- concluding whether policy belongs to state, provenance, or external context cannot be decided by convenience but is determined by transformation sufficiency (independently arriving at a question the parallel verifier track, S1602/S1603, was also attacking).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories have the same proposition but different validity intervals theta_A(p)=[t0,t1), theta_B(p)=[t1,t2). Suppose a transformation asks CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)? Then the two states produce different results. ... Temporal validity is not merely decorative metadata if temporal queries are
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-query counterexample (CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)?) that a state representation omitting temporal qualification fails congruence when temporal queries are valid operations -- confirming temporal validity is functionally load-bearing, not decorative metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e1->p and e2->not p. Compare K_A={p,e1} with K_B={p,e1,e2,not p}. A transformation T_assess may produce Assessment(K_A)=Supported but Assessment(K_B)=Conflicted. ... A state representation containing only the latest proposition K={p} would lose information necessary for future assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a contradictory-evidence counterexample showing evidence multiplicity is semantically relevant: two states differing only in whether conflicting evidence is retained produce different Assessment outcomes (Supported vs Conflicted) under T_assess, so a state keeping only the latest proposition would lose information needed for future assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose an information component x can affect the result of a valid future transformation T(K,i). Then x cannot be discarded from the state abstraction unless it is recoverable from other state information. Formally: x is semantically disposable => x=f(K) for some reconstruction function f, or no va
a_rows_sample.statement: States a general disposability criterion generalizing all the preceding counterexamples: an information component x may be discarded from the state abstraction only if it is reconstructible from the remaining state (x=f(K) for some f) or no valid operation can distinguish states differing only in x -- giving a formal test for classifying any candidate field as state, metadata, provenance, external context, or truly redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=F(H) is a transformation-sufficient representation if all permitted future semantics can be determined from K, rather than the complete H. But we should not call K a sufficient statistic without qualification. ... K must be sufficient for the permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit but qualified analogy to the statistical notion of a sufficient statistic: a state K=F(H) is transformation-sufficient if all permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics can be determined from K rather than the full history H -- but the file cautions the statistical term applies to a specific model/parameter and should not be borrowed unqualified, since the KnowledgeOS requirement is broader (sufficiency for a whole permitted transformation semantics, not one parameter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H ~ mu_H. Then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K = F_* mu_H. ... mu_K is a regime-level object, not necessarily part of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the state abstraction to measure theory without making it foundational: if H is a random history with distribution mu_H, then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K=F_*mu_H (mu_K(A)=mu_H(F^{-1}(A)) for measurable A); explicitly classifies mu_K as a regime-level object, consistent with the parallel Step 246 finding (S1601) that probability belongs to a regime projection, not to K itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F is a compression map. The question becomes: Is this compression lossless with respect to the semantics we care about? That is exactly the congruence question. ... F o That = T o F. This is the formal expression of state sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the commutative-diagram criterion F o That = T o F as the formal expression of state sufficiency (the state abstraction F is a compression map; sufficiency means the compression is lossless with respect to the transformation semantics), calling it one of the strongest formal tests obtained in the corpus so far, and gives the corresponding failure interpretation (a non-commuting diagram means the proposed state representation has lost necessary information).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Content,Qualification,Governance) survives the experiments only if those components contain all information required by valid transformations. ... we should not yet assert K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as a final decomposition. Instead: K must be defined by transformation sufficiency. This reverses
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the design question from 'what fields should a Knowledge State have?' to 'what information must a state preserve so that all valid KnowledgeOS transformations remain well-defined?'; explicitly withholds asserting K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as final until it survives transformation-sufficiency testing -- a route to the same skepticism about the 5-tuple that the parallel verifier track reached by counterexample.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality = systematic removal + congruence testing. This is far stronger than selecting the smallest-looking tuple. ... Minimality is always relative to the transformation language. ... Minimality(K) = Minimality(K | T). There may be no context-free 'minimal Knowledge State.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates minimality testing as systematic per-component removal followed by re-checking the congruence criterion (F^{-i} o That = T^{-i} o F^{-i}), rather than choosing the smallest-looking tuple by inspection; states the important architectural corollary that minimality is always relative to the transformation language T (Minimality(K)=Minimality(K|T)) -- there may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State, since a richer future transformation set can make previously-discardable information necessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition: T:K x I -> K is semantically well-defined with respect to That iff F(H1)=F(H2) => F(That(H1,i))=F(That(H2,i)) for all valid H1,H2,i. Equivalently F o That = T o F. ... not yet a proven KnowledgeOS theorem, because the full transformation set has not been estab
a_rows_sample.statement: States the phase's central named proposition (Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition), giving a single precise, computationally testable mathematical criterion for when a state-level transformation is semantically well-defined relative to a history-level one -- explicitly labeled not yet a proven theorem because the full KnowledgeOS transformation set has not itself been established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS -- Transformation congruence criterion established. FAIL -- Global state sufficiency not yet demonstrated. OPEN -- Minimal sufficient Knowledge State. ... K should not be defined independently of T. Instead, the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed together.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the Step-248 verdict: PASS on establishing the congruence criterion; FAIL on demonstrating global state sufficiency; OPEN on minimal sufficient K; states the phase's major conceptual shift -- K must not be designed independently of the transformation set T, but the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed jointly -- and sets Step 249 as Transformation Algebra Reconstruction, to derive the corpus-supported transformation classes (T_create, T_observe, T_infer, T_validate, T_revise, T_reject, T_merge, T_supersede, ...) with domain/codomain/preconditions/postconditions/invariants/composability for each.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can two states with identical current representation produce different valid future behavior? ... If T(K_A)=K'_A and T(K_B)=K'_B with K'_A not equiv K'_B, then history affects future semantics. In that case, the compressed state K is not sufficient. This gives us a rigorous state sufficiency criteri

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose they produce identical lineage edges. Yet the transformations had different policies pi_A != pi_B. a_rows_sample.statement: States the congruence condition required for the equivalence-class definition of Knowledge State to be usable: ~_H must be preserved by every valid transformation (H1~_H H2 => T(H1)~_H T(H2)), so that transformations descend consistently from histories to their equivalence classes -- directly foreshadowing S1608's F o That = T o F criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest mathematical structure that satisfies all non-negotiable requirements? Construct a sequence K0 -> K1 -> K2 -> ... where each added component must have a demonstrated necessity. ... a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a 'minimal adequate K' procedure: build up a sequence K0->K1->K2->... adding only demonstrably-necessary components (tested against 7 questions per candidate: forcing requirement, external representability, derivability, removal breakage, reconstructability, circularity, unwanted coupling), and introduces a 3-level minimality-confidence taxonomy (PROVEN / PLAUSIBLE / NOT ESTABLISHED) explicitly rejecting fewer-fields as a minimality argument -- complementing S1608's congruence-based removal test with a positive constructive procedure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot yet remove Merge, Supersede, Split, Withdraw because the corpus may require them for capabilities that have not yet been tested. Therefore the minimality status is: NOT YET TESTABLE rather than: minimal set found.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares minimality of the state-changing operation family NOT YET TESTABLE (not merely unresolved), since Merge/Supersede/Split/Withdraw cannot yet be safely removed given untested capability requirements -- consistent with S1608's mandate that minimality testing requires actual removal-and-congruence checks, not inspection.

b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit competing models for the fundamental KnowledgeOS object: Model A (state-sufficient, K_t alone suffices, history is external/reconstructable provenance) versus Model B (history-essential, the real object is a pair (K_t,H_t)) -- to be decided by whether two histories producing the same apparent state can remain semantically different.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If H_t = f(lambda_t), then history may not need to be a separate primitive. Instead: Lineage could be a sufficient compressed representation of history. ... (K_t,H_t) is unnecessary if K_t=(Content_t,lambda_t,...) already contains all semantically relevant historical information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the lineage-as-sufficient-compression hypothesis: if the full history H_t can be reconstructed from the lineage component lambda_t alone (H_t=f(lambda_t)), then the state-history pair (K_t,H_t) collapses back to a single sufficient state K_t=(Content_t,lambda_t,...), making lineage an important candidate compression of history rather than a separate primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `258.8` | `K_1 ≡_K K_2 ⟺ ∀O ∈ 𝒪: O(K_1)=O(K_2)` ... `261.5` | `K_1 ≈ K_2 ⟺ ∀O ∈ 𝒪_K: O(K_1)=O(K_2)` — **the identical formula** ... $$\boxed{\equiv_K \text{ and } \approx \text{ share one formula while being listed as distinct.}}$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers a critical corpus self-contradiction (later catalogued as gap G-67): loci 261.1 and 246 declare semantic equality (≡) and observational equality (≈) to be distinct and non-interchangeable, yet loci 258.8 and 261.21 define K1≡_K K2 as 'for all O in the observation set, O(K1)=O(K2)' -- and locus 261.5 gives the identical formula, 'for all O in O_K, O(K1)=O(K2),' as the definition of K1≈K2. b_rows_sample.anchor:
def expressive(F, predicates, space=SPACE):
    """Expressive(F, I): no two F-identified states disagree on any predicate."""
b_rows_sample.statement: Ground-truth executable definition of Expressive(F,I): for a given finite enumerated space of states, bucket states by their F-image, then check that no two states sharing an F-image disagree on any predicate in I; returns (bool, list of witnessing disagreements). This is the operational form of the Expressive conjunct used throughout the Sufficient(F,O,I) adoption argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathrm{Sufficient}(F,\mathcal O,\mathcal I)\;&:\Longleftrightarrow\; \mathrm{Congruent}(F,\mathcal O)\ \wedge\ \mathrm{Expressive}(F,\mathcal I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition proposed for adoption: for a state abstraction F with s1~F s2 iff F(s1)=F(s2), Congruent(F,O) requires every state-transforming operation in O to respect F-indistinguishability, Expressive(F,I) requires every mandated predicate/invariant in I to respect F-indistinguishability (i.e. Expressive is Congruence for the 0-ary/predicate case), and Sufficient(F,O,I) is their conjunction. Closes G-56 (previously open since the second-order pass, at 0 adoption).

type_signature.domain: state abstraction F, operation set O, predicate set I

b_rows_sample.anchor: Congruent ∧ ¬Expressive | `F₄ = K=(𝒜,ℛ)` ... Expressive ∧ ¬Congruent | `F₂ = content+status`
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed independence proof that Congruent and Expressive are neither redundant: witness (a) F4=K=(A,R) is Congruent=True but Expressive(I_merge_prov)=False against the section-265.11 merge-provenance invariant; witness (b) F2=content+status is Congruent=False (fails on Remove/Revise/Transform) but Expressive(I_any_accepted)=True. Both directions realized, so the conjunction Sufficient=Congruent AND Expressive is a proper (non-redundant) conjunction.
